Definition: from G3105; craziness:--(+ make) X mad.
BiblicalUsage: manía is madness, and it occurs once, in Acts 26:24. As Paul speaks for himself, Festus cries out with a loud voice, Paul, you are beside yourself, much learning makes you mad. The word is the world's verdict on a man speaking the truth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe manía warns me that the world will call faithful speech madness, and I hold that Paul's so-called madness was the sanest speech in the room.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
